heading: Helper calls in each language
body: JavaScript, TypeScript and Python use Behaviors.properties(CatalogSettings, values) and Behaviors.validate(Input, value). PHP uses Behaviors::properties(CatalogSettings::class, $values) and ::validate(Input::class, $value). Java and Kotlin use string names that Tachyon generates from the same source, for example Behaviors.properties("CatalogSettings", values). They do not use reflection. C# passes typeof(CatalogSettings). Swift passes CatalogSettings.self with try. Rust uses Behaviors::properties::<CatalogSettings>(&values)? and ::validate::<Input>(value)?. Go uses BehaviorsProperties[CatalogSettings](values) and BehaviorsValidate[Input](value). These factories are synchronous. In JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, C#, Dart and Swift, the cache, HTTP and query methods are async. In Java, Groovy, Kotlin, PHP, Rust and Go, these remotes are synchronous, with cooperative limits. With cooperative limits, the running code checks the limits itself. C# and Swift use BehaviorJSON. Rust uses BehaviorValue with BehaviorResult, and Go uses BehaviorValue with (BehaviorValue, error). The JVM (Java virtual machine) languages use strict native values that are compatible with JSON. Context creation keeps its current API, with optional profiles and properties. See docs/BEHAVIOR_ANNOTATIONS.md for the exact typed forms and for fixtures you can run.
